In [[mathematics]], the '''AKNS system''' is an [[integrable system]] of [[partial differential equations]], introduced by and named after [[Mark J. Ablowitz]], David J. Kaup, [[Alan C. Newell]], and Harvey Segur from their publication in [[Studies in Applied Mathematics]]:  {{harvs|txt|last1=Ablowitz|last2= Kaup|last3= Newell|last4= Segur|year=1974}}.

==Definition==

The AKNS system is a pair of two partial [[differential equation]]s for two [[complex-valued function]]s ''p'' and ''q'' of 2 variables ''t'' and ''x'':

:<math> p_t=+ip^2q-\frac{i}{2}p_{xx}</math>
:<math> q_t=-iq^2p+\frac{i}{2}q_{xx}</math>

If ''p'' and ''q'' are [[complex conjugate]]s this reduces to the [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]]. 

[[Huygens' principle]] applied to the [[Dirac operator]] gives rise to the AKNS hierarchy.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chalub |first1=Fabio A.C.C. |last2=Zubelli |first2=Jorge P. |title=Huygens' principle for hyperbolic operators and integrable hierarchies |journal=Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena |date=2006 |volume=213 |issue=2 |pages=231–245 |doi=10.1016/j.physd.2005.11.008 |bibcode=2006PhyD..213..231C |url=http://cmaf.fc.ul.pt/arquivo/docs/preprints/pdf/2004/2004024.pdf}}</ref>

== Applications to General Relativity ==
In October of 2021, the dynamics of [[(2+1)-dimensional topological gravity|three-dimensional (extremal) black holes on General Relativity with negative cosmological constant]] were shown equivalent to two independent copies of the AKNS system.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cárdenas |first1=Marcela |last2=Correa |first2=Francisco |last3=Lara |first3=Kristiansen |last4=Pino |first4=Miguel |date=2021-10-12 |title=Integrable Systems and Spacetime Dynamics |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.127.161601 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=127 |issue=16 |article-number=161601 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.127.161601|pmid=34723615 |arxiv=2104.09676 |bibcode=2021PhRvL.127p1601C }}</ref> This duality was addressed through the imposition of suitable boundary conditions to the [[Chern–Simons theory|Chern-Simons action]]. In this scheme, the involution of conserved charges of the AKNS system yields an infinite-dimensional commuting asymptotic symmetry algebra of gravitational charges.
